prints.texto: Admissions, spending and in-hospital mortality by year, with the jump in cost and mortality during the pandemic.
prints.alt: Overview page: 107.4 million admissions, R$ 151.73 billion spent, average cost of R$ 1,549 in 2023 and 6.61% mortality in 2021, with charts of admissions and spending by year and mortality from 2015 to 2023.

prints.texto: The 20 diagnoses with the most admissions and the highest cost, with average cost, length of stay and mortality.
prints.alt: Diagnoses page: bars of admissions and spending by diagnosis, with normal delivery first in volume and viral diseases (including COVID) first in spending, and a table with admissions, spending, average cost, days and mortality.

prints.texto: The main diagnoses year by year. The button at the top switches the measure between admissions, spending and mortality.
prints.alt: Trends page with ten small line charts, one per diagnosis, showing admissions from 2015 to 2023: fewer births, more heart attacks, sepsis and strokes and the COVID peak in 2021.

prints.texto: Yearly spending in R$ millions by diagnosis. COVID passes R$ 7.5 billion in 2021, and heart attack and sepsis rise almost every year.
prints.alt: Trends page with the Spending (R$ mi) measure: ten small line charts from 2015 to 2023, with the COVID peak in 2021 near R$ 8 billion and rising spending on heart attack, sepsis, stroke and chronic kidney disease.

prints.texto: In-hospital mortality by diagnosis. Pneumonia and COVID spike during the pandemic, while heart attack mortality falls from 11.7% to 8.2%.
prints.alt: Trends page with the Mortality (%) measure: ten small line charts from 2015 to 2023, with COVID above 20% in 2020 and 2021, the pneumonia peak in 2020 and the steady fall in heart attack mortality.

prints.texto: Admissions per thousand people per year, average cost, mortality and length of stay in the 27 states.
prints.alt: States page: bars of admissions per thousand people per year, with Paraná, Roraima and the Federal District at the top and Sergipe last, and a table with region, admissions, average cost, mortality and days.
